children: Unrest in France could have financial and fiscal repercussions, XTB research director Kathleen Brooks writes. Riots swept the eurozone's second-largest economy over the weekend. Some half a million protesters took to the streets, expressing anger at the high cost of living. The protests could widen the spread of French government bonds against German peers, and could also hit the euro, Brooks says. "If these riots boost support for the anti-EU Marine Le Pen, then we may see further declines for the single currency," she warns. (joshua.kirby@wsj.com; @joshualeokirby)
